mora_note: A long vowel and a diphthong may occupy two morae
basic_rules: Open syllables are strongly preferred in modern native and adapted words
Consonant + vowel is the default syllable, even if represented with one compact written cluster
Independent vowels are permitted at word start and hiatus
Two adjacent consonants are not automatically one syllable
Historical names and certain grammatical morphemes preserve consonant-final exceptions
Letter stacks are orthography, not an invitation to ignore the spoken CV structure
S, Z and SH are different: SH represents one fricative sound and does not trigger S/Z epenthesis
Attested legacy pronunciations override generic repair

historical_exception_policy.required: Do not respell inherited words or proper names against their recorded form
historical_exception_policy.spoken_repair: A transitional vowel can be pronounced without appearing as a separate Latin transliteration letter

consonant_contact.trigger: Two adjacent consonant phonemes without a written or dependent vowel nucleus

other_sibilant_pairs.where_C: Any consonant other than a vowel
other_sibilant_pairs.status: proposed default subject to historical lexicon
exclusions: Within a historically lexicalized compound with its own pronunciation

general_clusters.warning: A vowel selected by morphology or dictionary beats the default

gemination.example: llo represents a long L onset and an O nucleus, not three subscripts

stress.normal: Penultimate mora preferred in newer regular words, with lexical exceptions
stress.status: proposed adaptation of Māori mora-oriented stress

phonemic_conservation: All sound groups in alphabet-and-sounds.json remain pronounceable despite orthographic compression.

differentiation.spoken_syllable_phonemes: Can be 1 or more, independently of written cluster count

orthography: The roman letter u can remain in historical or English transliterations, but the modern native letter inventory has no independent U.
